page.title: Delivery matrix
page.purpose: Answer the operator's first question — which iOS targets can I prove right now, where will the work actually run, and what is blocking me.

priorities.statement: Terminal 'unsupported' rows are visually distinct from actionable 'unavailable' rows.
priorities.notes: This ramp has rows that will never go green. An operator who reads them as tasks will waste time trying to fix the unfixable.

priorities.statement: Every row states which node will execute the work.
priorities.notes: On a Linux host nothing runs locally. Hiding that makes a remote failure look like a local one.

priorities.statement: The build host's identity and toolchain version are visible from the matrix.
priorities.notes: Whether a build will be submittable depends on the fulfilling node's Xcode version, which is not a property of the artifact.

priorities.statement: A host that can validate but not produce submittable builds reads as its own state.
priorities.notes: Neither a pass nor a failure. Presenting it as either one misleads about a dated, foreseeable constraint.

states.description: The matrix as the live system reports it, with a macOS node online.
Target inventory is being probed; no dispositions are asserted yet.
No macOS node is reachable. Native targets are unavailable; the Linux-host rows remain unsupported. The two states appear together and must be distinguishable.
The build host's toolchain is below the App Store Connect floor. Simulator validation is available; producing a submittable build is not.
A required cell failed. The gate reads failed and names the contributing cell.

claims.statement: Unsupported and unavailable rows differ in shape or label, not only in colour, and unsupported rows offer no remediation affordance.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. Offering a 'fix this' control on a row that can never pass is an active lie. This is the most important assertion on the page.

claims.statement: Every non-terminal row names the node that will execute it.
claims.rationale: Remote execution is the normal path here, so 'where does this run' is part of reading the row, not a detail.

claims.statement: A build host below the SDK floor produces a distinct, explained state rather than a pass or a generic failure.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-004. The Intel build host will eventually reach exactly this condition, and it must be legible before an upload fails.

claims.statement: Every verdict on this page is perceivable without playing a recording.
claims.rationale: Journey video is evidence, not interface.
